B.N. Chowdhury with Kazi Ebadul Haq, Advocates ----- for the Petitioners 
Md. Golam Rabbani with Ranesh Chandra Maitra, Advocates ----- for the Opposite Party No. 1
parties:
Mosammat Nurunnahar Begum & Another
Vs.
Abdul Jabbar Mondal & Others
full_judgment: 11. Next, we come to the question of limitation. The undisputed legal position is that onus is upon the applicant seeking pre-emption to prove the date of knowledge if the applicant comes long after the usual period of limitation following execution and registration of the deed. In the instant case, the petitioner has come with his application for pre-emption 3½ years after the execution and registration of the deed and it has been alleged by the petitioner that he gathered knowledge from O. P. Dr. Nurul Haq and his brother who was O.P. No. 4. Both the courts below have found that as Dr. Nurul Haq was himself contesting the petition and as O.P. No. 4 was brother of Dr. Nurul Haq, it was not possible for the applicant to produce them as witnesses. We do not differ with this finding but it has appeared from the evidence of the applicant Abdul Jabbar Mondal P.W. 1 that when he learnt from Dr. Nurul Haq and his brother O.P. No. 4 about the transfer, his son was also present. The petitioner has not examined his son and no explanation has been advanced: as to why he has not been examined. The learned District Judge has not said a word about the non-examination of the son and the learned trial court has dismissed the question of non-examination by simply observing that the petitioner has not examined his son for "obvious reasons." We cannot but come to the conclusion that the petitioner has withheld his son whom he could easily bring as a witness in order to corroborate his assertion that he came to acquire knowledge of the transfer from Dr. Nurul Haq and his brother on 20.4.77. The learned courts below were entitled to make an adverse presumption that if the son was examined as witness, he would not have supported the P.W. 1 and in the circumstances of the case we are of the opinion that the courts below should have an adverse presumption. The learned courts have failed to exercise the jurisdiction drawn below vested in them by law in failing to draw an adverse presumption and to come to a conclusion that the petitioner has failed to prove the date of his knowledge and as such the application was barred by limitation.
